question: Which current Ordivon responsibilities are poorly carried by Agent cognition or ad-hoc reasoning, and which non-Agent entity types measurably improve the same owner-native workload without taking semantic or domain authority?
baseline: current owner-native mechanisms plus Agent judgment and simple deterministic scripts
decisionRule: Retain an entity role only when the same real workload exposes a failure or uncertainty that the candidate resolves more exactly, cheaply, independently, or observably than Agent-only/simple baselines. Do not infer a shared service from a useful role.
authorityBoundary: Owner repositories retain domain truth; Runtime retains physical execution truth; Host retains semantic continuity; Harness retains bounded Agent Run truth. Verifiers, optimizers, estimators, sensors, simulators, humans, and indexers may produce evidence or decision support but do not silently acquire owner authority.
nonScalarRule: Do not collapse the comparison axes into one universal score. Preserve Pareto/incomparability when different entities trade off distinct dimensions.
stopRule: Stop after every EG0-EG8 candidate has an evidence-backed retain/localize/defer/reject disposition and no shared service remains admitted only by conceptual elegance.
deletionRule: Experiment scripts may remain only if they are compact reproducibility equipment. Temporary databases and generated indexes are deleted after each run; durable conclusions remain in result JSON and this report.
